headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad write scopes make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, read/write files, and shares state via GitHub PRs/Slack threads; Goose shares state via filesystem and also uses MCP. That creates a plausible bridge for attacker-controlled content to flow from one agent into the other as instructions, even without a documented direct channel. The pathway is not provably blocked, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF either agent reads the other's generated text from a shared workspace, PR, Slack thread, or MCP output as instructions
IF an MCP server or file is used as a message bridge between the agents
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate workspaces
Disable shared MCP servers for the pair
Require human review before copying outputs between agents
Add provenance labels to all inter-agent artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation for instructions vs data

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, while Goose touches source code and files in cwd. Goose shares state via filesystem, and Devin has broad network egress plus Slack/Jira/Notion writes, so sensitive workspace data can flow outward if both operate on the same repository or directory. This is a default-plausible leakage path, not merely unusual configuration.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or working directory
IF either agent is given secrets, tickets, or chat content that the other can read from shared files
mitigations: Separate repositories or clones per agent
Remove secrets from shared working directories
Limit Devin's write scopes to only required integrations
Turn off filesystem sharing for Goose sessions
requires-engineering: add per-agent secret redaction at the workspace boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, package installation, and git-state modification. Goose explicitly shares state via filesystem, while Devin supports parallel sessions and shared integrations, so concurrent edits to the same repo can race and corrupt git state or files. The overlap is dangerous by default and can cause irreversible repository damage.
conditions: IF both agents are allowed to modify the same git branch or working tree
IF no external lock or merge gate serializes their writes
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Use a lock file or lease before writes
Require one agent to be read-only during the other's run
Pause parallel sessions on the same repo
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can act autonomously inside its workspace and write to GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion; Goose can make tool calls with user confirmation and also modify files. If Goose's output is treated as authoritative by Devin, or Devin's output is used to trigger downstream actions, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or messages without adequate verification. The pair therefore has a high-risk action chain.
conditions: IF one agent's output is fed into the other's task plan without a verification step
IF either agent is permitted to commit, message, or ticket based on the other's unreviewed output
mitigations: Require explicit verification before acting on peer output
Block direct auto-commit from either agent
Use a human approval step for external messages
Limit Goose to draft-only mode for shared tasks
requires-engineering: add structured output validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not state conflicting residency, certification, or retention regimes. Devin does handle team chat, issue trackers, and integration tokens, while Goose handles model provider keys and extension tokens, so compliance risk exists mainly if regulated data is routed through those integrations. Because no explicit mismatch is documented, this remains low and only one-agent citations are needed for the relevant handling surfaces.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Slack, Jira, Notion, or extension tokens
IF an operator routes data subject to residency or retention rules through either agent
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared integrations
Review retention settings for connected services
Rotate any exposed tokens
Use separate tenants for sensitive projects
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
